- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often lags 1–3 days in adjusting to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day delay in price correction when sentiment changes sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; reduce forecast amplitude in high-variance periods.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add a downward bias of 1–2% to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.2.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is weak (e.g., 0.0–0.3) — model tends to overconfidently predict rallies.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often overweights recent highs — apply a 1–3 day smoothing filter to reduce noise.
